clue.text: Firm's data, brief and easy to read, with one alteration

indicators.note: brief tells us to cut the word short, dropping its final letter

parts.note: data is information, shortened to INFO

indicators.note: one alteration means a single letter of the word is changed for another

parts.note: easy to read means legible

explanation.surface: A company boasting that its figures are concise, readable and only once revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' trims INFO to INF; 'with one alteration' swaps the G of LEGIBLE for an X, giving LEXIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something firm is rigid and unbending, a direct synonym.

clue.text: After lifting, doctors start to inspect foot

indicators.note: lifting in a down entry means reading upwards, reversed

parts.note: the BMA is the British Medical Association, the doctors' body

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Doctors begin examining a patient's foot after he lifts it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' is the metrical unit, not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot in poetry is a metrical unit; this one is an unstressed then stressed syllable.

clue.text: Chess manoeuvre on king's side?

parts.note: to be on someone's side is to be for them
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A chess move that supports the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on king's side' reads as for the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic where one piece attacks two enemy pieces at once.

clue.text: Head of equestrians amusingly holding on with reins?

indicators.note: head of means the first letter
holding means containing, wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: comically means amusingly

explanation.surface: A riding instructor jokes about holding on with the reins.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags 'with reins' as figurative: keeping a tight rein on spending, not on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a tight rein on money means spending thriftily and sparingly.

clue.text: Shooting fashionable friend

parts.note: in means fashionable
bud is American slang for a friend

explanation.surface: A stylish pal out on a shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' suggests guns but means sending out shoots.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant forming buds is beginning to sprout, putting out shoots.

clue.text: Passageways contain family allotments at the end, beanpole displaying this

indicators.note: contain means hold inside, enclose

parts.note: lanes are narrow passageways
kin is family

indicators.note: at the end means the last letter

explanation.surface: Allotment paths are lined with garden plots and canes for runner beans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beanpole' is a tall thin person, not the garden cane.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanpole is a tall skinny person, whose gangly thinness is the quality defined.

clue.text: Leader leaves source of water unaltered

indicators.note: the leader, the opening letter, departs from the word for a water source

parts.note: an oasis is a desert spring, a source of water

explanation.surface: A boss walks away from a spring and leaves it untouched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader leaves' removes the first letter of OASIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin-derived phrase means in the existing state, without changes.

clue.text: Text group in aquarium to make reservation

parts.note: a school is a group of fish
to book is to make a reservation

explanation.surface: Text message to a group booking a trip to the aquarium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Text' suggests a message, but it is a textbook.
explanation.definitionFit: A textbook used for lessons is a text.

clue.text: Filth from roof: it's seen in small landing area

indicators.note: seen in means placed inside

parts.note: a quay is a landing place for boats
a lid is a cover or roof

explanation.surface: Grime falling from a roof on to a small wharf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roof' is not the definition: 'from' links it to the wordplay, where a lid is the roof or top of a box.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirt and squalor, a state of filthy neglect.

clue.text: Dignitary backed by bank invested in horse that's added to stock?

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, here inside the horse

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: by means next to, so the bank comes beside the reversed dignitary

parts.note: a row is a bank or tier, as of seats or keys

indicators.note: backed means turned round, read from the end

parts.note: a nob is a dignitary or toff

explanation.surface: An investor's horse is somehow added to his holdings, like livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' looks like farm animals or shares, but it is the kitchen broth.
explanation.definitionFit: Bones with marrow are simmered by cooks to make soup stock, so this is a defining example.

clue.text: Pastry: it hurts when halves are swapped

indicators.note: the two halves of the word change places, front pair to the back

parts.note: ouch is what you say when it hurts

explanation.surface: A painful bit of baking, perhaps a burnt finger from the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when halves are swapped' turns OU|CH into CH|OU.
explanation.definitionFit: Choux is a light French pastry used for eclairs and profiteroles; the singular names one such bun.

clue.text: Food's dear in Paris, itinerant repeated to Mary

parts.note: cher is French for dear

indicators.note: itinerant means wandering, so the letters roam into a new order
repeated means the small word appears twice

explanation.surface: A wandering Mary has expensive meals in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated' doubles TO; 'itinerant' scrambles TOTO and MARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round salad variety eaten whole, an item of food.

clue.text: Occupants here supposedly forget it's a place without privacy

definitions.meaning: the fish kept in a glass bowl are popularly said to have a memory of seconds
a situation where everyone can watch what you do, like fish in clear glass

explanation.surface: Residents of somewhere so exposed that they prefer to forget it.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass fishbowl is literal home to forgetful fish and an idiom for a life lived in public view.

clue.text: Rising key, in the manner of politician

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
a la is French for in the style of
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A politician's speech style in a rising key.
explanation.definitionFit: Increasing step by step, growing in intensity or amount.

clue.text: Radio personality, one locally hugged by busy auxiliary

indicators.note: hugged by means enclosed by

parts.note: active means busy
a DJ is a disc jockey on the radio
'un is a dialect form of one

explanation.surface: A local radio host hugged by a busy assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locally' signals a regional dialect form, as in 'a good 'un'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean supplementary, added in a supporting role.

clue.text: Face the children, revealing minor affair

parts.note: a face of a cube or building is a side
issue is a legal word for offspring

explanation.surface: Confronting the kids turns up a small scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter of secondary importance, off the main point.

clue.text: Male wearing slip in work perhaps heading skywards?

definitions.text: Male wearing slip in work perhaps heading skywards?

indicators.note: in means placed inside the reversed word
in a down entry heading skywards means read upwards, reversed

parts.note: an opus is a work, as of music

indicators.note: wearing means clothed by, so the slip goes round the male

parts.note: to err is to slip up
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A caped hero in tights flying up from the office.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a costumed man soaring upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A costumed comic-book figure who flies through the sky is the picture the whole clue paints.

clue.text: Burning tar, clear on the outside

indicators.note: the word for clear goes round the other piece

parts.note: to clear a place of something is to rid it
a tar is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman)

explanation.surface: Hot tar being scraped off the outside of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tar' looks like the sticky stuff but is the old word for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean fierce and furious, as in burning or raging zeal.

clue.text: Island's atmosphere captivating British in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the assembled word is read in reverse
captivating means holding captive, enclosing

parts.note: an aura is an atmosphere about a place or person

explanation.surface: An island charm that wins over retired Britons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captivating' puts B inside AURA to make ABURA, which 'in retirement' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean island off the Venezuelan coast, part of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

clue.text: Tom perhaps with fine implement cut back hedge

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, an example of a pussy
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: back means read in reverse
cut means lose the final letter

parts.note: a tool is an implement

explanation.surface: A cat watches the gardener trim a hedge with a fine tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' shortens TOOL to TOO, and 'back' turns it to OOT. 'hedge' looks like the garden noun but is the verb, to avoid commitment.
explanation.definitionFit: To hedge is to be evasive and avoid committing, the same as tiptoeing around an issue.

clue.text: Increase of speed shown by small group having reduced time during warfare

indicators.note: during means within, so the pieces sit inside the warfare word

parts.note: action is fighting, warfare

indicators.note: reduced means cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a cell is a small group, as of activists
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Wartime speeds up as a small unit runs short of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown by' and 'having' are link words; the trimmed cell and the era sit just after the first two letters of the warfare word.
explanation.definitionFit: The physics term for a rate of gaining speed, here the gain itself.

clue.text: Egyptian king is upset to see another African

parts.note: Tut is short for Tutankhamun, the boy pharaoh

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned upside down, reversed

explanation.surface: A pharaoh is distressed at seeing another person from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bantu people of Rwanda and Burundi; the Egyptian is African too, hence another.

clue.text: Daughter breaks close relationship up for change

indicators.note: up in a down entry means read upwards, reversed
breaks means cutting into the word

parts.note: a tie is a close bond

explanation.surface: A daughter breaking up a close relationship for a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' puts D in TIE; 'up' reverses TIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise or alter a text is to change it.

clue.text: European's lifted in all the best meat

indicators.note: lifted in a down entry means moved higher up within the word

parts.note: vale is Latin farewell, all the best

explanation.surface: A European eats only the finest cuts of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted in' moves the E of VALE upwards, two places nearer the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The flesh of a calf, a type of meat.

clue.text: Both limos regularly used in American region

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: Two stretch limousines routinely employed somewhere in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: A Midwestern state of the USA, a region of America.

clue.text: Riders do such sprints back in base outside of Lille

indicators.note: in means put inside the base word

parts.note: a bed is a base or foundation, as in a bed of concrete

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: darts are quick sprints or dashes

indicators.note: outside of picks the first and last letters of the city name

explanation.surface: Cyclists sprinting back to base near the French city of Lille.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riders do such' is the definition: what any rider does to a horse or bike.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit astride a horse or bicycle with legs either side is what any rider does.

clue.text: Safety vest clothing Frenchman?

indicators.note: clothing means wearing, so the letters sit inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A man in France pulls on a hi-vis safety jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: one French first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A common French first name, as in Yves Saint Laurent, so one Frenchman.

clue.text: Unopened sausage, mostly porky — centrepiece of lunch in that flat

indicators.note: unopened means without its opening letter

parts.note: chorizo is a spicy Spanish sausage

indicators.note: the centrepiece is the middle letter of the five-letter word
mostly means all but the final letter

parts.note: porky is rhyming slang (pork pie = lie), so a tall tale

explanation.surface: A butcher's lunchtime spread: a sausage and a fib, in a London flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unopened' drops the C of CHORIZO; 'mostly' trims TALE to TAL. PORKY is British rhyming slang: pork pie = lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying level and parallel to the ground is being flat.
